definitions.explanation: The written text of a play, film, TV show, or other performance, containing dialogue, stage directions, and scene descriptions.

examples.japanese: {台本|だいほん}を{読|よ}んで{練習|れんしゅう}する。
examples.english: I practice by reading the script.

examples.japanese: {監督|かんとく}が{台本|だいほん}を{書|か}き{直|なお}した。
まるで{台本|だいほん}があるかのように{話|はなし}が{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: Things progressed as if there were a script.

notes:
Used for scripts in theater, TV, film, and radio. Can also be used figuratively to suggest something feels planned or staged.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {台本|だいほん}を{書|か}く — to write a script
- {台本|だいほん}{通|どお}り — according to the script
- {台本|だいほん}を{覚|おぼ}える — to memorize the script
- {台本|だいほん}{読|よ}み — script reading (rehearsal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {脚本|きゃくほん} — screenplay, script (more formal, emphasizes the written work)
- シナリオ — scenario, screenplay (loanword, also used figuratively)
